easy.def: Dry food for pets.
examples: The dog ate kibble.
Kibble is pet food.
The kibble is crunchy.

more.def: Dry, hard pellets of food for dogs and cats.
examples: The dog crunched its kibble.
Kibble is poured into the bowl.
She scooped kibble into the cat's dish.

easy.def: To hit something with your foot.
examples: Kick the ball.
He kicked the can.
I kick my feet in the pool.

more.def: To hit or push something with your foot.
examples: She kicked the ball into the net.
Swimmers kick their feet to move through water.
He kicked off his muddy boots.

easy.def: A hit with your foot.
examples: The kick was strong.
He gave the ball a kick.
A kick sent the ball over the fence.

more.def: A strike with the foot.
examples: A strong kick sent the ball over the fence.
The goalie stopped the penalty kick.
Her swimming kick is strong and steady.

easy.def: A game like baseball where you kick the ball.
examples: We play kickball at recess.
Kickball is fun.
I kicked the ball in kickball.

more.def: A game like baseball in which players kick a large rubber ball instead of hitting it with a bat.
examples: We play kickball at recess on the playground.
In kickball, you kick the ball and then run around the bases.
Our class had a kickball game on the last day of school.

easy.def: The kick that starts a game.
examples: The kickoff is at two.
We watched the kickoff.
The kickoff began the game.

more.def: The kick that starts a football or soccer game, or the start of any event.
examples: The kickoff is at two o'clock.
The crowd cheered at the kickoff.
The fair's kickoff was a parade.

easy.def: A small stand that holds up a bike.
examples: He put down the kickstand.
The kickstand holds the bike.
The kickstand is metal.

more.def: A small metal stand on a bicycle or motorcycle that holds it up when parked.
examples: He kicked down the kickstand and parked.
The bike leaned on its kickstand.
The kickstand broke.

easy.def: A child.
examples: The kid ran fast.
Every kid got a toy.
A kid sat by me.

more.def: A child, in everyday talk.
examples: The kid next door has a pet turtle named Pickle.
Every kid in the class made a drawing of the sea.
When I was a kid, I loved to climb trees.

easy.def: A baby goat.
examples: The kid ran to its mom.
A kid ate hay.
The goat had a kid.

more.def: A young goat.
examples: The little kid hopped around the barnyard on wobbly legs.
The goat stayed close to her new kid.
A kid can walk soon after it is born.

easy.def: A body part that cleans your blood.
examples: You have two kidneys.
The kidney cleans blood.
The kidneys are in your back.

more.def: One of two organs in your body that clean waste from your blood.
examples: You have two kidneys in your back.
A kidney cleans waste from the blood.
Drinking water helps your kidneys work.

easy.def: To make something stop living.
examples: Frost can kill a flower.
Too little water kills plants.
The cold killed the grass.

more.def: To cause a living thing to die.
examples: A very hard freeze can kill the tomato plants in the garden.
Some medicines kill the germs that make us sick.
Lack of rain killed many trees during the drought.

easy.def: A person who spoils other people's fun.
examples: Do not be a killjoy.
He is a killjoy.
The killjoy ended the game.

more.def: A person who spoils other people's fun.
examples: Don't be a killjoy; let us play.
He was a killjoy who ended the party early.
The killjoy sighed at the noise.

easy.def: A very hot oven for clay.
examples: The pots bake in a kiln.
A kiln is hot.
The kiln makes pots hard.

more.def: A very hot oven that makes clay hard.
examples: The potter put the bowl in the kiln.
A kiln bakes clay until it is hard.
Bricks are baked in a kiln.

easy.def: A short word for a way to say how heavy something is.
examples: It weighs a kilo.
The bag is a kilo.
I bought a kilo of rice.

more.def: A short word for a kilogram, a unit of weight.
examples: The bag of apples weighed one kilo.
She bought two kilos of potatoes.
A kilo is a little more than two pounds.

easy.def: A way to say how heavy something is.
examples: The bag weighs a kilogram.
A kilogram is heavy.
I bought a kilogram of apples.

more.def: A unit of weight equal to one thousand grams.
examples: The bag of flour weighs one kilogram.
A baby elephant can weigh over a hundred kilograms.
I bought two kilograms of apples.

easy.def: A unit for measuring distance, about six tenths of a mile.
examples: The school is a kilometer away.
We walked a kilometer.
The road is ten kilometers long.

more.def: A unit of length in the metric system equal to one thousand meters, or about six tenths of a mile.
examples: The park is one kilometer away.
We walked five kilometers on the trail.
A kilometer is about six tenths of a mile.

easy.def: A knee-length skirt with pleats worn by men in Scotland.
examples: He wore a kilt.
The kilt is plaid.
A kilt has pleats.

more.def: A knee-length pleated skirt made of plaid cloth, worn in Scotland.
examples: The piper wore a plaid kilt.
A kilt is part of a traditional Scottish outfit.
He wore a wool kilt to the festival.

easy.def: A long, loose robe from Japan.
examples: She wore a kimono.
The kimono is silk.
The kimono is colorful.

more.def: A long, loose robe with wide sleeves that is a traditional dress in Japan.
examples: She wore a silk kimono to the festival.
The kimono was tied with a wide sash.
Her kimono had pink flowers on it.

easy.def: Your family and relatives.
examples: We visited our kin.
My kin live far away.
Her kin came for dinner.

more.def: A person's family and relatives.
examples: We visited our kin during the holiday.
My kin live on a farm in the countryside.
Her distant kin came from all over the country for the reunion.

easy.def: Nice and caring to others.
examples: It is kind to help a friend.
The kind nurse gave me a sticker.
Be kind to animals.

more.def: Friendly, gentle, and caring about how others feel.
examples: A kind stranger helped us find our lost dog.
It was kind of you to share your umbrella.
Her kind words made me feel better.

easy.def: The first year of school, for five-year-olds.
examples: I am in kindergarten.
My sister starts kindergarten.
We play games in kindergarten.

more.def: The first year of school, for children around five years old, before first grade.
examples: My sister starts kindergarten this fall.
In kindergarten, we learned to write our names.
The kindergarten class sang a song at the assembly.

easy.def: A child in kindergarten.
examples: Ben is a kindergartener.
A kindergartener is five.
The kindergartener drew.

more.def: A child who goes to kindergarten, the first year of school.
examples: My sister is a kindergartener.
The kindergarteners sang a song.
A kindergartener learns letters.

easy.def: Kind and caring.
examples: A kindhearted girl.
The kindhearted nurse.
A kindhearted man.

more.def: Having a kind and caring nature.
examples: The kindhearted nurse comforted the child.
A kindhearted neighbor brought soup.
She is a kindhearted girl who helps everyone.

easy.def: To start a fire.
examples: He kindled a fire.
They kindled the stove.
She kindled the logs.

more.def: To start a fire burning, or to make a feeling grow.
examples: He kindled a small fire with dry twigs.
The story kindled her love of books.
They kindled the campfire with matches and dry leaves.

easy.def: Small sticks used to start a fire.
examples: We need kindling.
Kindling burns fast.
I gathered kindling.

more.def: Small dry sticks or twigs used to start a fire.
examples: We gathered kindling to start the campfire.
The kindling caught fire first.
Dad split wood into kindling.

easy.def: In a kind way.
examples: She smiled kindly.
He kindly helped us.
Please speak kindly.

more.def: In a kind and caring way.
examples: She smiled kindly at the shy girl.
He kindly helped us carry the bags.
The nurse spoke kindly to the child.

easy.def: Being nice to others.
examples: Thank you for your kindness.
She showed kindness.
Kindness is important.

more.def: The quality of being friendly, generous and caring toward others.
examples: Her kindness to the stray cat made the neighbors smile.
She showed kindness to the new student.
A small act of kindness can make someone's day.

easy.def: Related or alike.
examples: They are kindred spirits.
Kindred friends.
A kindred soul.

more.def: Alike in spirit or character, or related by family.
examples: The two friends were kindred spirits who loved the same books.
They felt a kindred bond.
She found a kindred soul at the club.

easy.def: A man who rules a country.
examples: The king lives in a castle.
The king wore a gold crown.
Long ago, a king ruled the land.

more.def: A man who rules a country and usually comes from a royal family.
examples: The king and queen waved from the castle balcony.
In many old stories, the king has a magic sword.
Kings used to wear heavy gold crowns.

easy.def: The main piece in chess.
examples: The king can move one square.
Keep your king safe.
He moved the king.

more.def: In chess, the piece that must be protected; if it is trapped, the game is lost.
examples: In chess, you win when you trap the other player's king.
A king can move only one square at a time.
She moved her king out of danger.

easy.def: A land with a king or queen.
examples: The queen ruled a big kingdom.
The kingdom had a tall castle.
A dragon lived in the kingdom.

more.def: A country that is ruled by a king or queen.
examples: Everyone in the kingdom came to the castle for the feast.
The news spread across the whole kingdom.
The young prince would one day rule the kingdom.

easy.def: A bird with bright blue feathers that dives for fish.
examples: A kingfisher sat by the river.
The kingfisher dived.
I saw a kingfisher.

more.def: A small, brightly colored bird with a long beak that dives into water to catch fish.
examples: A kingfisher perched on a branch above the stream.
The kingfisher dived and came up with a silver fish.
Kingfishers flash blue as they fly low over the river.

easy.def: Like a king.
examples: He walked in a kingly way.
A kingly robe.
The kingly lion.

more.def: Fit for a king; grand and noble.
examples: The lion walked in a kingly way.
He wore a kingly robe.
The kingly feast filled the hall.

easy.def: Being a king.
examples: His kingship began.
The kingship was long.
Kingship is rule.

more.def: The position or rule of a king.
examples: His kingship lasted for forty years.
The prince was ready for kingship.
The old story told of the king's kingship.

easy.def: A bond like family.
examples: We feel kinship.
They share a kinship.
Kinship ties us.

more.def: A feeling of closeness like that between family members.
examples: We feel a kinship with the other team.
The two friends share a close kinship.
Kinship among neighbors helped in hard times.

easy.def: A small booth where things are sold.
examples: The kiosk sells maps.
A kiosk is on the corner.
I bought a drink at the kiosk.

more.def: A small open booth where newspapers, snacks or information are given out.
examples: I bought a magazine at the kiosk.
The kiosk in the park sold ice cream.
A tourist kiosk gave out maps.

easy.def: To touch with your lips to show love.
examples: Mom kissed my cheek.
I kiss my dog on the nose.
Grandpa kisses us goodnight.

more.def: To touch someone or something with your lips to show love or care.
examples: She kissed her baby brother on the forehead.
The little girl kissed her teddy bear.
He kissed the bruise on his sister's knee to make it feel better.

easy.def: A touch with your lips to show love.
examples: Give Grandma a kiss.
Dad blew me a kiss.
The baby gave the puppy a kiss.

more.def: A gentle touch of the lips to show love or to say hello or goodbye.
examples: She gave her mother a kiss before the bus came.
He waved and blew a kiss from the train window.
The toddler planted a wet kiss on my cheek.

easy.def: A set of tools or things used for something.
examples: We have a first aid kit.
I got a craft kit.
The model kit has ten pieces.

more.def: A set of tools or parts used for a certain purpose.
examples: Dad keeps a first aid kit in the car.
I built a model plane from a kit.
The art kit has paint and brushes.

easy.def: The room where food is cooked.
examples: Mom cooks in the kitchen.
The kitchen smells good.
We eat in the kitchen.

more.def: A room where food is prepared and cooked.
examples: Grandma baked bread in the kitchen.
We washed the dishes in the kitchen sink.
The restaurant kitchen was busy at dinner.

easy.def: A very small kitchen.
examples: The apartment has a kitchenette.
The kitchenette is tiny.
We cooked in the kitchenette.

more.def: A small kitchen, often part of another room.
examples: The hotel room had a kitchenette.
We made toast in the kitchenette.
The kitchenette had a tiny stove.

easy.def: Things used in a kitchen.
examples: The kitchenware is clean.
Kitchenware includes pans.
We bought kitchenware.

more.def: Pots, pans, utensils and other items used for cooking.
examples: The store sells kitchenware.
She bought new kitchenware for her apartment.
Kitchenware includes pots and spoons.

easy.def: A light toy that flies in the wind on a string.
examples: We flew a kite.
The kite is red.
My kite hit the tree.

more.def: A light toy made of paper or cloth on a frame that flies high in the wind when you hold its string.
examples: We ran across the field and let the red kite climb high into the wind.
The kite's long tail danced as it flew over the beach.
I tied a new string to my broken kite and fixed it.

easy.def: A kind of bird that hunts with long wings.
examples: A kite flew over the field.
The kite has a forked tail.
We saw a kite in the sky.

more.def: A bird of prey with long wings and a forked tail that glides on the wind as it looks for food.
examples: A kite glided over the fields, looking for mice in the grass.
The kite's forked tail helps it steer as it flies.
We watched a kite circle high above the hill.

easy.def: A baby cat.
examples: The kitten is tiny.
I have a kitten.
The kitten plays with yarn.

more.def: A very young cat.
examples: The kitten chased a ball of yarn.
Our kitten sleeps in a basket.
The mother cat had four kittens.

easy.def: A small white sea gull.
examples: A kittiwake flew.
The kittiwake is a gull.
I saw a kittiwake.

more.def: A small sea gull with white feathers and black wingtips that nests on cliffs.
examples: A kittiwake nested on the cliff.
Kittiwakes spend winter at sea.
The kittiwake calls its own name.

easy.def: A little cat.
examples: The kitty is soft.
I pet the kitty.
The kitty drinks milk.

more.def: A kitten or cat, a word used by children and when speaking in a loving way.
examples: The kitty curled up on my lap and purred.
She calls her cat kitty because it is small and fluffy.
Here, kitty, kitty, time for dinner!

easy.def: A small fruit with green inside and a fuzzy brown skin.
examples: I ate a kiwi.
The kiwi is green inside.
Kiwi is sweet.

more.def: A small, oval fruit with fuzzy brown skin and bright green flesh.
examples: I scooped the green inside out of a kiwi.
The kiwi was sweet and a little sour.
Kiwi slices lay on top of the cake.

easy.def: A brown bird from New Zealand that cannot fly.
examples: A kiwi is a bird.
The kiwi cannot fly.
We saw a kiwi.

more.def: A small, round, brown bird of New Zealand that cannot fly and has a long beak.
examples: The kiwi hunts for insects at night.
A kiwi cannot fly, but it can run fast.
The kiwi has a long, thin beak.
